entries.title: One menu, one Home, and each action in one place
entries.summary: Navigation rebuilt: one menu on every screen, a Home that shows what needs your signature, old links redirected.
details: Home replaces the old Dashboard, Operations and landing pages and opens on the transactions that need your signature.
Desktop and phone share one menu: Home, Create CLIQ, Validator, Settings, Audit & tests and Guides. Settings now holds the old Account page.
Old links keep working: Operations, Account and the chain page redirect, checked with real requests against a production build.
Duplicate buttons were removed, such as the many Create buttons, a second Vote tile on the validator page and repeated copy and explorer buttons on the CLIQ page.
Unused code was removed: a hidden alternative transaction form and 21 files nothing used.
Wallet and transaction signing code is unchanged, proven by a hash check over 63 files and 85 signing functions.
The validator page no longer claims an existing validator can be moved into a CLIQ; that was checked against TX's own chain code.
Verified: 69 test suites and 608 tests pass, plus type, lint and format checks and a production build.

entries.title: One-click Unjail on the validator page
entries.summary: A jailed validator can now be unjailed with one click from its dashboard, for shared and single wallets alike.
details: Adds an Unjail action inside the jailed banner on the validator dashboard, shown only while the validator is actually jailed.
The button stays disabled, with a plain-language notice, when the validator can never be unjailed or while the jail period is still running.
Works for both shared (multisig) operators, who get a transaction to sign, and single-wallet operators, on every supported chain.
Verified with 63 test suites and 460 tests, all passing (2 new suites, 36 new tests), plus type checks, lint with zero warnings, and formatting checks.
Nine deliberate code breaks each turned the matching tests red, confirming the tests genuinely guard the feature.

entries.title: JSON editor upgraded, clearing all six of its advisories
entries.summary: The JSON editor was upgraded, clearing all six of its known security advisories.
details: The JSON editor component was upgraded to a major new version, moving its underlying framework to a release with no known advisories.
Verified: 61 test suites, 424 tests all pass; build, lint, type and formatting checks pass; 6 advisories cleared and none added.
Checked side by side in the browser against the old editor: identical editing, error highlighting and form updates.
The editor's download shrank from 148 KB to 127 KB compressed.

entries.title: Four more dependency security advisories patched
entries.summary: Four more known dependency weaknesses, all in build and test tooling, were patched; none reach users.
details: Patched four tooling dependencies used only for linting, testing and building; none of them ship to the browser.
Verified: 61 test suites, 424 tests all pass; build, lint and formatting checks pass; 6 advisories cleared and none added.
The built styles are byte-identical before and after, and the same 403 files pass lint.

entries.title: All open critical and high dependency alerts fixed
entries.summary: All 11 open critical and high dependency security alerts were fixed with small, in-range updates.
details: Cleared all 11 open critical and high dependency alerts using patch releases and lockfile-only updates; no other package changed version.
The app framework stays on its current major version; every update stays inside the range already allowed.
Verified: 61 test suites, 424 tests all pass before and after; build, lint and formatting checks pass.
13 dependency advisories cleared (2 critical, 10 high, 1 moderate); none added.
A local smoke test confirmed the site serves and image processing works after the update.

entries.title: Crawlers and AI readers now get real robots.txt and llms.txt
entries.summary: The site now serves proper robots.txt and llms.txt files to search engines and AI readers.
details: robots.txt and llms.txt previously returned the app's HTML page; real plain-text files are now served.
Verified on a local server: both files return text/plain and match the committed files byte for byte.
A break test (temporarily removing the file) confirmed the check can fail; restoring the file made it pass again.
Lint and build checks pass; normal page routing is unchanged.

entries.title: Servers must run a current Node version and report it
entries.summary: The required Node.js version was raised to 20.19, and the health check now reports the version in use.
details: Raised the declared minimum Node.js version to 20.19 in both places the service can be built from, matching what its dependencies need.
The health endpoint now includes the Node version in every response, so one request shows whether the deployed engine is new enough.
Verified with syntax and formatting checks plus a clean-room install and full test gates, all green.

entries.title: Transaction details are no longer embedded in page HTML
entries.summary: Transaction pages no longer embed amounts, recipients and memos in the HTML; data loads via a rate-limited route.
details: The page's server-rendered HTML previously carried the transaction's full details; it now returns only the transaction id.
Details are fetched by the page itself through a rate-limited route, now the single place this read exists.
A new test asserts no memo, amount, recipient, hash or signer address appears in the page data; 414 tests across 59 suites pass.

entries.title: Destructive actions are now recorded in a tamper-evident log
entries.summary: Wipe, export, send and cancel actions are now recorded in a per-multisig log that detects tampering.
details: A new log records what happened for the wipe, export and send/cancel routes, including refused destructive attempts with the reason.
Fifteen tests prove the write completes, the entries chain correctly per multisig, and both edited and deleted entries are detected.
Tests confirm each multisig's events stay in its own space, and only a fingerprint of the payload is stored — never amounts, recipients or memos.
Verified: 414 tests across 59 suites pass, plus type, lint and formatting checks.

entries.title: Emergency rollback rehearsed against the live site
entries.summary: The production rollback was rehearsed live end to end: zero downtime in either direction, measured to the second.
details: Rolled the live site back one deployment and forward again, sampling it once per second: 58 samples, all successful responses.
Measured: the switch completes in 3–4 seconds and the target build starts serving within about 7 seconds; zero failed responses either way.
The drill found a brief window where old and new builds serve side by side, so the runbook now requires sampling for 15 seconds to verify a switch.
The runbook now requires a revert or a merge freeze after any rollback so the same change cannot be shipped again.
